standard_prerequisites.name: Characterization of Dedekind domains by the discrete valuation property of localizations
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that the localizations of the integrally closed B at maximal ideals are discrete valuation rings.

standard_prerequisites.name: The glueing situation for one-dimensional semi-local rings
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the ambient hypotheses relating A, B, K and R.

core_obligations: Treat the special case where B is integrally closed in K: conclude that B is a Dedekind domain, list its maximal ideals m_1, ..., m_r, and set R_1 = A times_K B_{m_1} (proof lines 7459-7466).
Verify that A tensor over R_1 with B_{m_1} still maps onto K, which is what allows the two-sided glueing to proceed with the local factor (proof lines 7466 onwards).
Complete the construction and the verification of the open-immersion and covering statements for R, up to line 7506, and reduce the general case to the integrally closed one.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the case where B is integrally closed, hence Dedekind.
Build the intermediate ring from A and one local factor of B.
Verify the tensor product surjectivity and conclude the glueing statements.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for two one-dimensional Noetherian semi-local domains A, B inside a common field K with A tensor B mapping onto K, the spectra of A and B are open subschemes covering Spec(R) and K equals A tensor_R B. The proof starts with the special case where B is integrally closed in K, i.e. B is Dedekind with maximal ideals m_1, ..., m_r, and builds the intermediate ring R_1 = A times_K B_{m_1}, verifying that the tensor product over R_1 with the localization still maps onto K and then descending the open-immersion statements to R (proof lines 7459-7466 and the following body up to line 7506). H2: the construction of the intermediate ring and the verification of the tensor product surjectivity are the substance; the general case is then reduced to the integrally closed one.
